fix: and at last, still not taught a lesson by Fortune, had advanced so far
reason: οὔπω νουθετούμενοι = not yet admonished by Fortune; English inverted the negation.

fix: For his own part, he said, he was ready to do this, because experience had taught him that
reason: ἕτοιμός εἰμι omitted; restores the ἐγὼ μὲν half of the contrast.

fix: Let Hannibal, Scipio said, put himself in Scipio’s place and say: should the Romans remove the harshest of the imposed terms,
reason: σὺ τὴν ἐμὴν χώραν μεταλαβὼν εἶπον: Hannibal takes Scipio’s place; persons were reversed.

fix: once they go into battle having given up all hope of life.
reason: ἀπελπίσαντες τοῦ ζῆν = despairing of life, not of everything except fighting.

fix: [...] of Masinissa’s men, the Carthaginian left wing was quickly stripped of its cavalry.
reason: Lacuna before τῶν περὶ τὸν Μασαννάσαν; ‘by this’ invented. Marked with [...]; construction of the genitive is lost.

fix: no one using comparable equipment could have arranged a better engagement against the Romans than the one Hannibal then arranged
reason: χρώμενον is accusative singular, the generic general, not the Romans.

fix: was now returning to it at more than forty-five years of age
reason: ἔχων + years gives age: he returned aged over forty-five, not after forty-five years away.
